subject.title: fix(reef): keep routine agent replies from disappearing

question: Should Reef adopt this broader default-allow guard rubric for signed peer task requests, or retain a narrower review/deny posture until a larger adversarial corpus is approved?
rationale: The change intentionally shifts Reef's prompt-injection and DLP boundary; tests can verify implementation but cannot choose the permanent product security posture.

options.title: Approve broader rubric after proof
options.body: Accept ordinary signed-peer task requests once lifecycle cleanup and an inspectable adversarial two-peer proof demonstrate bounded behavior.

options.title: Keep ambiguous tasks in review
options.body: Route more task-like or meta-instruction cases to owner review, reducing false-negative risk at the cost of more interrupted collaboration.

options.title: Pause the guard rewrite
options.body: Land no classifier broadening until a security owner defines a larger policy corpus and acceptance threshold.

recommendation.title: Approve broader rubric after proof
recommendation.body: Accept ordinary signed-peer task requests once lifecycle cleanup and an inspectable adversarial two-peer proof demonstrate bounded behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The self-assigned author owns the complete Reef change and is best positioned to confirm the intended collaboration-versus-guard tradeoff with security review.
